target.title: feat(mcp): requester-scoped MCP server connections
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #106229. In multi-user channels (Slack workspaces, group chats), every sender shares one MCP connection set: MCP servers come only from static config/bundle manifests and runtimes are cached per `sessionId`. Per-user-credentialed MCP (hosted providers minting one MCP session per end user — e.g. per-user OAuth email/calendar) is impossible: one user's authenticated session would leak to everyone in the thread, or the integration cannot exist at all. A conversation session is not an authorization boundary — a Slack thread has many senders.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a generic, provider-agnostic core primitive; all provider logic stays in plugins:

- **New plugin API:** `api.registerMcpServerConnectionResolver({ serverName, resolve })`. Server *identity* stays static (`mcp.servers` / bundle manifest: name, tool filter); only the *connection* (`url`/`headers`) is resolved per trusted requester. `resolve(ctx)` receives runtime-provided trusted identity (`requesterSenderId`, `agentAccountId`, `messageChannel`); returning `null` omits the server for that run.
- **Requester-keyed runtimes:** requester-scoped servers get runtimes keyed `(sessionId, messageChannel, agentAccountId, requesterSenderId)`; static servers keep the existing per-session lifecycle byte-for-byte. Sessions with no registered resolvers are entirely unchanged.
- **Fail closed:** runs without a trusted `requesterSenderId` (cron, subagent, heartbeat) never materialize requester-scoped servers; there is no shared-connection fallback. `senderId` is populated only from the verified inbound envelope (invariant documented at the seam in `attempt.ts`).
- **Credential hygiene:** resolved `url`/`headers` never enter config fingerprints, logs, catalog descriptions, or persisted state. Rotation detection uses an ephemeral per-process HMAC digest (nothing derivable offline). Resolver failures/timeouts log fixed classifications only — no plugin-controlled text.
- **Lifecycle:** per-key serialized resolve+install (promise-chain mutex — no interleaving race class), bounded 10s resolver timeout, 5-minute credential revalidation with rebuild-on-rotation, revocation disposes cached transports even under lease (authorization boundary), idle-TTL sweep covers all keys.
- **Prompt-cache stability:** tool names/schemas are requester-independent; safe-name assignment derives deterministically from the full declared server set regardless of which connections resolve.

Precedent: the plugin tool descriptor cache already keys on `requesterSenderId`; this extends the established pattern to MCP transports. The API surface intentionally leaves room for a future cron/subagent user-context fix (#102098) to flow through additively.

**Note for reviewers (surface changes):** no new `openclaw.json` keys or env vars. Plugin SDK gains one registration method + 3 public type exports; `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` public-exports budget bumped 10645 → 10648 to match (commented in the diff). `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` regenerated per the check's documented flow.

## User Impact

Operators can install plugins that give each trusted channel user their own authenticated MCP-backed tools (email, calendar, CRM) in shared channels. Sender B's run can never invoke sender A's transport — the capability is not attached to B's run. Existing configurations see zero behavior change. Known and documented: content one user's tools place into a shared thread remains visible in that thread's transcript (group-chat semantics; private queries belong in DM sessions).

## Evidence

- Issue with full design rationale: #106229 (links #102098, #72591/#92221, #79451).
- Validation (Blacksmith Testbox + local focused runs): `pnpm check:changed` lanes green (format, SDK baseline, SDK exports, surface budget, lint); `tsgo` + `tsgo:test` exit 0; focused suites `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime`, `mcp-connection-resolver`, `agent-bundle-mcp-tools.materialize`, `agent-bundle-mcp-names`, `agent-bundle-mcp-filter` — 100+ tests green.
- Six rounds of structured adversarial review (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning) drove the hardening above: resolver timeout/error containment, revocation-disposes-under-lease, per-key serialization replacing three interim concurrency guards (net −70 LOC in the manager), HMAC digest instead of plain credential hash, constant catalog descriptions, SSE alias preservation, lease aggregation for requester-only sessions, safe-name-map fingerprint participation.
- Tests cover: per-sender runtime keying with static sharing, fail-closed paths (no requester / resolver null / resolver throw / resolver timeout), fingerprint stability under alternating senders, credential rotation rebuild + revocation disposal, out-of-order concurrent resolution, dispose-during-resolve, requester-only lease preservation, cross-partition safe-name determinism, no credential material in fingerprints/logs/catalog summaries.

Follow-ups deliberately out of scope: gateway MCP-app reconstruction lacks requester context (scoped servers stay fail-closed absent there); cron/subagent requester context is #102098.

Written with AI assistance; reviewed and directed by @obviyus.
